result.summary: READ-ONLY review of target d428e0f730ed5649485732e95d39c32f5d6a8895 (feature/binary-config-serve-20260930), scope: 50/400-worker operational limits (scheduler complexity, provider/model backpressure, per-worker locks, event loop/resource bottlenecks). Verdict FINDINGS: 2 HIGH, 3 MEDIUM, 1 LOW. HIGH-1 src/security.ts:5/43 - Redactor.text() calls secrets() per string, re-running SELECT body FROM workers + JSON.parse per row and (3+workers)*3 replaceAll passes; Redactor.value() recurses per field, so one list_workers page costs 1013ms of synchronous CPU at 400 workers, a coordinator tick costs 821ms (vs a 2000ms poll interval) and the 1s event-log flush costs 1291ms. HIGH-2 src/metrics.ts:100 - three full events-table scans per worker per scrape; events.worker_id is unindexed (src/store.ts:27, EXPLAIN shows SCAN events); render = 253.6ms at 400 workers/2000 events. MEDIUM-3 src/coordinator.ts:340/397 - no concurrency cap on provider/agent fan-out (measured peak 400 concurrent getWorker). MEDIUM-4 src/providers/opencode.ts:116 + src/coordinator.ts:544 - full session history refetched per poll plus a usage UPSERT per historical assistant message (tick 359.5ms at 400x60). LOW-5 store.all() rescanned twice per tick/per spawn; LOW-6 src/coordinator.ts:373 O(VMs x workers) scan. All reproduced with fake provider/agent and real local SQLite only; no real cloud/model/VM. Report: /workspace/.swarmforge/artifacts/review.md; /workspace/.swarmforge/artifacts/findings.json.
result.details:
Setup: disposable detached clone at /tmp/sfrev/tmprepo, verified `git rev-parse HEAD` = d428e0f730ed5649485732e95d39c32f5d6a8895. /workspace/repo left at assigned baseline 5672ead2a526e07fea9ed11e58b3725e42013527, clean, unmodified. Snapshot Bun 1.3.14 cannot read lockfileVersion 2, so official Bun 1.4.2 was installed to /tmp/bun142; the lockfile was never rewritten.

F1 (HIGH, src/security.ts:5 + :43-50, value at :24-37; hot callers src/coordinator.ts:650-651,707, src/runtime.ts:185,198, src/mcp.ts:40, src/http.ts:42, src/files.ts:70,103,135): redactorFor returns a lazy closure over store.all(); text() invokes it per string, so each redacted string is a full workers-table scan plus (3+workers)*3 replaceAll passes (1209 at 400 workers). Reproduced: list_workers page of 100 = 79.4/474.9/1013.5 ms at 50/200/400 workers; one tick() = 33.7/68.5/268.7/821.3 ms (superlinear) at 50/100/200/400 with only 5 messages per snapshot and an unchanged excerpt; eventLogger first flush = 1291.5 ms against setInterval(flush,1000) at src/serve.ts:193. Fix: memoize the secret set, one prebuilt alternation regex, and hoist secrets() into value().

F2 (HIGH, src/metrics.ts:81/100/111/121 + src/store.ts:27): three full events scans per worker per scrape; no index on events.worker_id. EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN returns [SCAN events, USE TEMP B-TREE FOR GROUP BY]. Metrics.render() = 9.1/67.9/253.6 ms at 50/200/400 workers using only 5 events per worker. Fix: index events(worker_id,type,at), aggregate per team, store run_id as a column instead of json_extract.

F3 (MEDIUM, src/coordinator.ts:340-352 and :397-400): Promise.allSettled/Promise.all fan out over every active worker; exclusive() serializes per worker ID only. Instrumented fake provider: recover() at 400 workers = 400 getWorker calls, peak 400 concurrent. Fix: bounded pool (16-32) plus 429 backpressure.

F4 (MEDIUM, src/providers/opencode.ts:116-129 and src/coordinator.ts:544-554): inspect() walks all older 100-message pages every poll, and monitor() issues a usage UPSERT per assistant message every poll. SQLite side measured: tick = 359.5 ms at 400 workers x 60 messages. HTTP page fan-out is code-evidenced only.

F5 (LOW, src/coordinator.ts:172,316,363; src/metrics.ts:74; src/mcp.ts:262,277): store.all() = SELECT body + JSON.parse per row, 0.35ms@50 to 1.68ms@400 rows, called twice per tick and once per spawn.

F6 (LOW, src/coordinator.ts:373-377): all.find(vm_id) inside the VM loop = 160k comparisons per reconcile at 400x400, while a byId Map is built one line later.

Not reported: the waitForStateChange synchronous event scan measured benign (2.8ms/800 rows), and per-worker lock semantics were read but left to the lifecycle reviewers.

Why no guard catches these: tests/helpers.ts:20 sets SWARMFORGE_MAX_WORKERS=2 and SWARMFORGE_MAX_PROVISIONING=1, so no test builds a list longer than two workers; redaction tests assert correctness (tests/api.test.ts:142) not cost, tests/excerpt.test.ts supplies its own redact callback and never reaches Redactor, and there is no render/flush/timeout budget assertion anywhere.

Artifacts: /workspace/.swarmforge/artifacts/review.md, /workspace/.swarmforge/artifacts/findings.json. Probes (disclosed, disposable, outside the checkout): /tmp/sfrev/probe/p1-redactor.ts, p2-redact-payload.ts, p3-metrics.ts, p4-tick.ts, p5-recover.ts, p6-wait.ts.

tests.summary: Targeted repo tests: 44 pass, 0 fail, 157 expect() calls, exit 0. Suite runs at SWARMFORGE_MAX_WORKERS=2 so it exercises no scale path. Probes used real SQLite plus fake provider/agent doubles only, no network to any provider and no VM: F1 reproduced (list page 1013.5ms, tick 821.3ms, log flush 1291.5ms at 400 workers), F2 reproduced (253.6ms render; EXPLAIN SCAN events), F3 reproduced (peak_concurrent_provider_requests=400), F4 partially reproduced (359.5ms tick at 400x60; HTTP fan-out code-evidenced), F5 reproduced (store.all 1.68ms@400), F6 code-evidenced.

warnings: Reviewer probes live only in /tmp (clone /tmp/sfrev/tmprepo at target d428e0f, probes /tmp/sfrev/probe, local SQLite files, Bun 1.4.2 at /tmp/bun142); /workspace/repo is untouched at the assigned baseline.
No real cloud/model provider or VM was contacted and SWARMFORGE_RUN_SMOKE was not used; provider-side effects in finding 3 are inferred from code plus a fake-provider concurrency count, not observed.
Absolute timings come from one container with a warm page cache; the worker-count ratios and the EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN output are the load-bearing evidence.
F4's HTTP page-fan-out half is code-evidenced only (the fake agent bypasses client.session.messages pagination).
Packaging/build, settings/config-serving, Git handoff and CLI scopes were not reviewed; the full test suite was not run.
SWARMFORGE_MAX_WORKERS has no upper bound in the config schema, so 400-worker behaviour is reachable by configuration alone; findings 1-3 were demonstrated at that scale.
